--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.bethe_hessian_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Get the Bethe Hessian matrix of an undirected graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.bethe_hessian_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Get the Bethe Hessian matrix of an undirected graph. title: >- [Graph.bethe_hessian_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get the Bethe Hessian matrix of an undirected graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the Bethe Hessian matrix of an undirected graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L90126-L90214){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.bethe_hessian_matrix( r=None, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Bethe Hessian matrix](../assets/graphs/bethe-hessian-matrix.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same five-node graph with degree badges and its Bethe Hessian at the default r = 1.67 (32 / 12 - 1, from the degrees). Each edge gives -r = -1.67 and the diagonal (accent) holds r² - 1 + degree: 3.78 for A, 4.78 for B, C and D, and 2.78 for E. At r = 1 it would be the Laplacian." width="100%"} The Bethe Hessian `H(r) = (r² - 1) I - r A + D` (Saade, Krzakala & Zdeborová, 2014) is a regularized Laplacian built for community detection in large sparse networks, where ordinary spectral methods break down: there, the number of its negative eigenvalues estimates the number of communities, and the corresponding eigenvectors reveal them. At `r = 1` it is exactly the Laplacian. The default `r` is the average excess degree `Σ d² / Σ d - 1` (unweighted degrees), as in NetworkX's `bethe_hessian_matrix()`; Saade et al. recommend its square root, which you can pass explicitly. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [r]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The regularizer. If `None` (default), uses `Σ d² / Σ d - 1`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether the adjacency and degree terms use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[float]], list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(matrix, node_ids)`: the matrix as a list of rows, and the node IDs labelling rows and columns, in increasing order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, or `r=` is omitted on a graph without edges. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~bethe_hessian_spectrum`) : The eigenvalues of this matrix. [](`~laplacian_matrix`) : The matrix this one is at `r = 1`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} At `r = 1` the Bethe Hessian is the Laplacian: ::: {#c5eb2ff1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec import polars as pl path = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) bethe, nodes = path.bethe_hessian_matrix(r=1) labels = [path.get_label_from_id(n) for n in nodes] pl.DataFrame(bethe, schema=labels, orient="row").insert_column( 0, pl.Series("node", labels) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

The default `r` comes from the degrees, and the many friends of the instructor and the administrator push it up to 6.77. Each friendship gets `-r`, and the diagonal `r² - 1` plus the member's number of friends: ::: {#3b14df29 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() bethe, nodes = karate.bethe_hessian_matrix() labels = [karate.get_label_from_id(n) for n in nodes] i, j = labels.index("0"), labels.index("1") round(-bethe[i][j], 2), [ round(bethe[k][k] - karate.get_degree(nodes[k]), 2) for k in (i, j) ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (6.77, [44.82, 44.82]) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#853f817b .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.plot(size_by="degree", label_by="label", seed=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
